subject.title: Agent loop allows simulated tool calls instead of enforcing real tool invocation

question: Should OpenClaw make structured `toolCall`/`toolUse` protocol objects the only default executable tool boundary, or keep the current standalone assistant-text promotion for local-model compatibility?
rationale: Current main deliberately combines diagnostic-only handling for unstructured fake-tool text with an executable promotion path for certain standalone text formats, and changing either side affects both security posture and local-model compatibility.

options.title: Strict protocol by default
options.body: Make assistant text non-executable by default and move any text repair behind an explicit provider compatibility path with warnings and regression coverage.

options.title: Keep compatibility promotion
options.body: Retain standalone text promotion as supported behavior and narrow this issue to docs, warnings, and better forced-tool-choice guidance.

options.title: Defer to response gates
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader pre-response enforcement design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/13583 instead of changing the tool-call boundary now.

recommendation.title: Strict protocol by default
recommendation.body: Make assistant text non-executable by default and move any text repair behind an explicit provider compatibility path with warnings and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame points to this owner across the current runtime promotion, diagnostics, and documentation surfaces.
